title: YOUR GRUMBLING IS AGAINST THE LORD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses also said, 'You will know that it was the LORD when he gives you meat to
eat in the evening and all the bread you want in the morning, because he has
heard your grumbling against him. Who are we? You are not grumbling against us,
but against the LORD.'" - Ex 16:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses repeats himself, and the repetition is deliberate. He wants this to land.

But notice something remarkable in the middle of it. God has heard their
grumbling, and His response is to give them meat in the evening and bread in the
morning.

Read that again. He heard the complaint, and He fed them anyway.

There is a mystery in God's dealings here that we should not flatten. Later in
the wilderness, grumbling brings serious consequences (Num 11:1). Here it brings
bread. God is not inconsistent; He is patient, and He knows the difference
between the panic of a hungry people early in the journey and settled rebellion
after years of proven faithfulness.

That should make us careful about two errors. We should not assume God is
indifferent to how we speak about Him. And we should not assume He is waiting to
punish us the moment we falter.

Peter writes that the Lord is patient, "not wanting anyone to perish" (2 Pet
3:9). His patience is not weakness. It is purposeful, and it has an end, but
while it lasts it is genuine kindness.

He heard, and He fed them. That is who He is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you assumed God is angry with you when He has actually been patient?
2. How do you speak about God when you are frustrated with your circumstances?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You hear my complaints and often answer with kindness.
Guard my mouth, and thank You for Your patience with me. Amen.
